question: How do I tell whether this house has polybutylene supply pipe before my inspection period ends?
verdictConfirmed: Look where supply pipe is exposed (water heater, main shutoff, under sinks, basement or crawl space ceiling); copper or PEX at the stub-outs does not clear the house, because inspections report visible material only.

facts.claim: Our report engine flags houses built 1978 through 1996 for a polybutylene check, says to look at the water heater and main shutoff, describes it as flexible and usually gray, sometimes blue or black, and puts a whole-home repipe at $4,000 – $15,000.
facts.quote: minYear: 1978, maxYear: 1996 ... howToCheck: 'Ask your inspector to check at the water heater and main shutoff. Polybutylene is flexible and usually gray, sometimes blue or black.' ... typicalRepairCost: 'Whole-home repipe $4,000 – $15,000'

facts.claim: 2021 IRC Table P2906.5 (water distribution pipe) lists CPVC, CPVC/AL/CPVC, copper, PEX, PEX-AL-PEX, PEX-AL-HDPE, galvanized steel, PE-AL-PE, PE-RT, polypropylene and stainless steel; polybutylene is not listed.
facts.quote: Table P2906.5 Water Distribution Pipe: CPVC; CPVC/AL/CPVC; copper or copper-alloy pipe and tubing; PEX; PEX-AL-PEX; PEX-AL-HDPE; galvanized steel; PE-AL-PE; PE-RT; polypropylene (PP); stainless steel -- no polybutylene entry

facts.claim: ASTM D3309 is the specification for polybutylene hot- and cold-water distribution systems; its scope includes methods of marking. The last edition, D3309-96a(2002), was withdrawn in 2010 with no replacement (the 1996 edition's page shows 'Historical' because the 2002 reapproval superseded it).
facts.quote: D3309-96a page: 'Standard Historical ... This specification covers requirements, test methods, and methods of marking for polybutylene plastic system components'. D3309-96a(2002) page: 'Standard Withdrawn, No replacement ... Last Updated: Dec 31, 2010 ... (Withdrawn 2010)'

facts.claim: Jana Laboratories / University of Illinois at Chicago paper: early PB failure attributed to chlorine; failures of both PB pipe and acetal fittings reported.
facts.quote: The early failure of polybutylene (PB) piping systems has been attributed to accelerated degradation due to chlorine in potable water (3,4). Failures of both the PB piping and the acetal fittings used in these systems have been reported (3,10).

facts.claim: Texas inspectors must report the visible material used for water supply lines (22 Tex. Admin. Code § 535.231(a)(1)(A)(iv)).
facts.quote: visible material used for water supply lines and drain lines;

facts.claim: Texas standards of practice: the inspection is a limited visual survey; not required to inspect anything concealed or use destructive testing (22 Tex. Admin. Code § 535.227).
facts.quote: is a limited visual survey and basic performance evaluation of the systems and components of a building ... is not intended to be a comprehensive investigation or exploratory probe ... any method employing destructive testing that damages otherwise sound materials or finishes ... anything buried, hidden, latent, or concealed
